waste_categories.description: Includes bottles, bags, packaging, containers, and other petroleum-based synthetic materials that do not decompose naturally for hundreds of years.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Rinse containers before recycling. Sort by resin code (PET, HDPE, PVC, LDPE, PP, PS). Take to a plastic recycling facility or curbside recycling bin (blue bin in most municipalities).
waste_categories.recommendation: Reduce single-use plastics, prefer reusable bottles/bags, and choose products with recyclable packaging codes 1, 2, or 5.
suggestions: Carry a reusable shopping bag
Switch to a steel or glass water bottle
Avoid buying over-packaged products
Donate or repurpose sturdy plastic containers

waste_categories.description: Biodegradable waste such as food scraps, vegetable peels, garden waste, and other kitchen leftovers that decompose naturally.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Compost at home using a compost bin or pit. Municipal wet-waste collection often converts this into compost or biogas at processing plants.
waste_categories.recommendation: Segregate wet waste from dry waste at source and compost wherever possible to reduce landfill load.
suggestions: Start a kitchen compost bin
Use vegetable peels as garden mulch
Avoid food wastage through meal planning
Use community composting facilities if available

waste_categories.description: Discarded electronic devices like phones, batteries, chargers, computers, and other electrical appliances containing hazardous heavy metals.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Never dispose of e-waste in regular bins. Drop off at authorized e-waste collection centers or manufacturer take-back programs where components are safely dismantled and recycled.
waste_categories.recommendation: Repair or donate working electronics instead of discarding them; recycle only through certified e-waste handlers.
suggestions: Locate your nearest certified e-waste center
Wipe personal data before recycling devices
Sell or donate still-functional gadgets
Avoid throwing batteries in household trash

waste_categories.description: Includes newspapers, cardboard boxes, office paper, magazines, and packaging material made from wood pulp.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Flatten cardboard boxes, keep paper dry and free from food contamination, and place in dry-waste/paper recycling bins.
waste_categories.recommendation: Reuse paper for notes/packing before recycling, and buy recycled-content paper products.
suggestions: Use both sides of paper before discarding
Flatten boxes to save recycling bin space
Shred sensitive documents before recycling
Avoid wet or greasy paper in recycling bins

waste_categories.description: Bottles, jars, and glass containers that are 100% recyclable without loss of quality, made from sand, soda ash, and limestone.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Rinse and separate by color if required locally (clear, green, brown). Drop at glass recycling bins; avoid mixing with ceramics or mirrors.
waste_categories.recommendation: Reuse glass jars for storage before recycling; glass can be recycled indefinitely.
suggestions: Reuse jars for storing spices or leftovers
Handle broken glass carefully and wrap before disposal
Don't mix window glass or mirrors with bottle glass
Return bottles to deposit-return schemes if available

waste_categories.description: Chemicals, paints, pesticides, medical waste, and other substances that are toxic, corrosive, flammable, or reactive.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Never mix with regular trash. Take to designated hazardous waste collection events or facilities for safe treatment and disposal.
waste_categories.recommendation: Buy only the quantity needed, store safely, and use community hazardous-waste drop-off days.
suggestions: Store chemicals in original labeled containers
Never pour chemicals down the drain
Return expired medicines to a pharmacy take-back program
Use eco-friendly cleaning alternatives when possible

waste_categories.description: Includes cans, foil, scrap metal, and other ferrous or non-ferrous metal items that are highly recyclable.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Rinse food cans, crush if possible, and place in metal/dry-waste recycling bins or sell to scrap dealers.
waste_categories.recommendation: Recycle metal repeatedly as it retains quality; consolidate scrap metal for local scrap collection.
suggestions: Rinse out cans before recycling
Collect aluminum foil separately and ball it up
Sell larger scrap metal to certified scrap dealers
Avoid mixing metal with general waste
